An environment-file edit does not revoke a running verifier. Compromise revocation is effective only when the verifier actually consumes the new generation; no live-reload claim is made. No Bridge-key, process-bearer or bootstrap-token alias is permitted in either direction: class 9 cannot mint a Bridge token. A boot/provisioning receipt records the selected signer and configured trust generation, including unselected trust kids as cleanup candidates. Expected configuration is distinct from the MC's live consumed-generation witness; one Fleet's observation cannot prove that no other process holds a private key.

**Atomic authority.** One GraphService-owned operation uses its existing physical SQLite connection and `.immediate()`, with no precommit Store mutations. It validates the typed state, reads revision/receipt and any transaction-owned fence, then commits episodes/corrections, revision and receipt together. `syncCache` consumes committed GraphLog invalidations afterward; max-log acknowledgement is not a substitute. Return `accepted`, `idempotent` or `conflict`. Episodes and corrections remain the family authority; receipts are operation evidence, not another era ledger. The snapshot reader obtains complete membership and declaration/correction populations plus revision in one read transaction, then detaches/freezes them and derives the temporal identity classification. Unavailable storage is not a successful empty map.

The common graph write boundary must also protect reserved admission identities/types and existing admitted records/relations, including durable receipts, from ordinary creation, relabelling, merge, deletion and decay, including cold rows. Trusted code custody authorizes the typed writer; a JSON `admitted: true` flag does not. Source-controlled roster seeding and approved migration/recovery retain their separate authorities.


## Issuer identity, trust consumption and provisioning history

**Q1 — stable issuer.** The trust leaf binds each allowed `kid` to one stable Fleet issuer for the plane. MC selects within that issuer's declared key set, never by trying every configured key. A signed different issuer is refused before receipt lookup. MC durably fixes the issuer at first admitted reservation under the proposed L3 lineage below; the original C4 first-trust-consumption pin is thereby moved earlier, not removed. A later configuration naming another issuer is a named unavailable/recovery state, not a fresh idempotency namespace. Key rotation retains the issuer.

**Q2 — provenance and cross-run reservation.** Host records remain the authority for each run's prior consent and effects. The proposed L3 plane lineage below is the authoritative cross-run reservation index for this credential class; it does not replace those records. “None consumed” is insufficient: a declaration can already exist. A staged but never consumed key remains create-once custody, and its loss never authorizes replacement.

| Plane lineage / target observation | Host generation evidence | Proposed L3 disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Supported empty lineage, valid phase-one boot descriptor, no recovery/restore fence or contradictory prior-generation evidence | The original host run records the selected attempt before minting | MC may atomically reserve that attempt; no key is generated until the host reads that exact admitted reservation. |
| Exact admitted reservation; current execution has not attempted generation | Intact original attempt record positively shows generation was never dispatched | Permit the one generation effect, recording it before mint/stage. No fingerprint is asserted before the key exists. |
| Reserved or consumed attempt | Intact private custody matches the recorded/bound generation | Recover and pair-check; never recompose random input. |
| Reserved attempt, possibly generated; pending, failed, interrupted or unknown host effect | Missing/partial/mismatched custody | Reconcile or refuse to named recovery authority; do not mint again. |
| Supported empty lineage | Prior class-9 effect/custody or an outstanding restore/recovery fence | Conflict/unknown; refuse automatic enrollment. An empty graph is not evidence that external authority disappeared. |
| Any lineage | A different proposed issuer/attempt, changed bytes under a bound kid, or a new run pretending to be a new generation | Refuse; explicit rotation/recovery is separate. A repeated identical reservation remains idempotent. |
| Unsupported, unreachable, unreadable, malformed or wrong-target observation | Any | Unknown: refuse to mint. |

Refusal/unknown rows take precedence. The first row depends on L3's boot-owned authority and an enforceable restore boundary, still OQ3; it is not a general empty-state permission. Target binding checks plane identity and expected data root. Secret-free descriptors carry attempt, issuer/kid and, **after generation**, the public fingerprint and custody references; never private key bytes. Host run IDs remain provenance, not generation authority.

**Current source supports pieces, not this complete table.** At Brain [`533724f0`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/tree/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b):
- [`applyEffect`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/fleet/hostEffects.mjs#L413) persists `pending` before the handler and reconciles interrupted attempts. Its generic failed-receipt and changed-input paths can invoke a handler again: class-9 create-once admission must guard those paths explicitly.
- [`retireCurrentProof`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/fleet/setupRunRecord.mjs#L302) preserves history **within one run**. [First-run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/scripts/setup/firstRun.mjs#L499) otherwise mints a run UUID and reads that one record. A fresh empty record cannot certify target-wide absence. `findReceipt` reads current receipts, and `withReceipt` replaces the same effect ID; neither supplies immutable generation history. Institution's [shell resume selector](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/blob/ee6ab02b6b744ff002bfa97a76a56e23c8fb5386/harness/setupBroker.mjs#L108) skips unreadable records, treats a directory-read failure as an empty list, and its fresh-run path creates another empty record. That UI selection is not completeness evidence.
- [Ordinary deploy](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/examples/cloud-deployment/deploy-pipeline.sh#L252) serializes materialize → recreate/health → delivery receipt under a host lock, with a new run UUID. Those records currently bind prescriptions/environment, not signer-generation history.
- [Redeploy preflight](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/scripts/maintenance/redeployPreflight.mjs#L117) already distinguishes declared initialization from destroyed/relocated state using independent prior-state evidence. Its absence rules are a precedent; they are not a class-9 witness.

**Required ownership extension.** CLI, shell and ordinary update must resolve the same target-bound lineage before any generation effect. Under the preferred L3 candidate the index is in MC; L1's host-reference alternative remains in the matrix below. A new run references the existing attempt and never creates authority by becoming a new run. Preserve generation identities/dispositions independently of replaceable current-effect receipts.

**First ordinary update — recommended sequence.** Preserve C3's next-ordinary-update outcome using two resumable phases in the **same** update, rather than requiring a second operator update:
1. After normal survivability preflight, deploy the class-9-capable verifier in an unprovisioned mode when upgrading a verified pre-class-9 composition. Existing provisioned trust must never be cleared to enter this path. The interim composition carries the non-secret reservation descriptor and must boot without a nonexistent signer-file mount; publication remains unavailable.
2. Read the supported, authenticated, plane-id/data-root-bound lineage witness. It must confirm the exact boot-admitted reservation; reconcile any host prior-effect evidence. Old or absent responses never authorize minting.
3. With the selected attempt already reserved, persist the generation-effect attempt before mint/stage, recover the same generation on resume, then stage the Fleet-only signer mount and MC public trust.
4. Recreate the affected services with the final composition, observe consumed generation and Fleet signer/trust agreement, then emit the final delivery result. An interim health success is not completion.

This is a proposed extension to existing first-run/update owners. The two phases need distinct durable effect identities and same-target serialization; the generic `compose-up` receipt must not accidentally skip the second phase. Interruptions resume by observation, never by re-mint. C7 freezes the proposed reservation, reconciliation and fence contract for version-bound graduation review; it does **not** certify implementation or installed readiness. “Update after a verifier-capable update” remains Ada's alternative; it weakens the original delivery promise and is not silently substituted.

## OQ3 carrier alternatives retained for the convergence read

[Ada's plane-held lineage](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/discussions/811#discussioncomment-19187787) supplies the missing cross-run index. It must be declared before the host mints; a later run reads the same plane record even when the earlier host run is unavailable. Two details in that proposal need revision: the first reservation cannot contain a fingerprint for a not-yet-generated key, and possession of the existing bootstrap PAT does not already authorize this protected mutation.

| Carrier / authority | When this would be right | Evidence / falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| **L1. Host-held lineage with a stable target reference** | Every supported setup/update/restore preserves and selects the same host history. | Fresh run selection currently does not prove coverage. Moving surviving plane volumes to a reprovisioned host loses that reference; absence must refuse, not mint. This can be safe but leaves that recovery unavailable. |
| **L2. Plane lineage declared by an authenticated provisioner API** | A separately specified server-side provisioner authority admits the typed reservation before generation. | Ordinary PAT validation is not that authority. [AuthService](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/mcp/server/shared/services/AuthService.mjs#L1001) installs ordinary bearer auth; its AuthInfo has identity/provenance, no provisioner role. The local profile disables the first-subject pin. An ordinary seat PAT must not reserve the plane signer. |
| **L3. Plane lineage admitted from the trusted MC boot configuration** | The existing host provisioner already controls MC's config generation and ordinary recreation; no additional mutation API is needed. | MC composition consumes a strictly typed reservation descriptor through an ADR-0019-owned leaf, atomically admits it to protected graph state, and exposes only a read witness. Falsified if a request caller can write that leaf/record, boot overwrites a different prior attempt, or graph unavailability is treated as an empty lineage. |

**Author recommendation: L3**, retaining Ada's plane-held carrier while using the config-generation authority already required for verifier trust. This is the selected direction in C7's proposed convergence, not a shipped primitive or completed graduation. L2 remains viable only with an explicit authorization and credential-reuse decision. A claim that unauthorized reservation “only blocks a mint” does not waive authorization: it can durably deny legitimate provisioning or constrain issuer selection.

**Proposed L3 state/order.** The host has two separate effects, `class9.reserve` and `class9.generate`, each with a durable dispatch record before its side effect. Before generation, reserve stages a non-secret boot descriptor containing attempt, stable issuer/kid and immutable `originRunId`; it contains **no public-key fingerprint yet**. During phase-one startup, an MC-owned lifecycle path atomically admits that descriptor to protected graph state: absent lineage may reserve it, identical reservation is idempotent, competing attempt/issuer conflicts. The host generates only after a fresh target-bound witness confirms its exact reservation and the original attempt record proves generation was not dispatched. It durably stores the private key, derives its public fingerprint, and phase two binds those bytes once to the same attempt/kid through the trusted public-key config. Changed bytes under a bound kid conflict; rotation is a separately admitted next generation under the same issuer.

The witness states are `unadmitted` (graph not ready), `reserved(attempt)`, `bound(attempt,kid,fingerprint)`, `fenced`, and `conflict`. A generation dispatch needs the exact `reserved` state and the positive original-record condition above. A retry already at `bound` reconciles custody and completion; it does not generate again. An unreadable/unsupported witness remains unknown. A reservation is not a signing credential, and neither a read witness nor a public-key request body installs trust.

**Original-record relation, not another host-wide ledger.** MC retains `originRunId` as non-secret provenance beside the attempt. Every later CLI/shell/update run resolves that original record through the canonical host setup root and [`setupRecordPath`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/fleet/setupRunRecord.mjs#L170), verifies target/attempt, and reads current **and retired** class-9 dispositions. It must not create a new empty record at that ID when it is missing. Its own fresh run is not a replacement. The class-specific generation disposition survives recipe retirement and generic same-effect receipt replacement; extending the existing record for this is required. If the original history is missing/unreadable or the setup root changes, “never generated” is unknown. An interrupted/failed generation recovers and pair-checks existing custody or refuses to named recovery authority. An already bound matching key can be recovered without granting any right to mint a replacement.

**Lost acknowledgement and head comparison.** Each pending phase records its expected previous lineage head and exact intended next head. A plane head equal to that pending target is the normal lost-acknowledgement arm, reconciled by fresh observation plus the phase's custody checks. It does not require a new generation or an operator recovery merely because the host has not recorded the reply. An unexplained head divergence fences the capability; “host behind” alone does not diagnose rollback. Cross-witnessed heads detect some one-sided divergence, but not histories and custody rewound consistently together or every family-data change within a generation. The [three constructive traces](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/discussions/811#discussioncomment-19188013) retain these limits; they are protocol counterexamples, not production tests.

MC's existing [boot-seed source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/memory-core/GraphService.mjs#L261) shows code-owned graph writes at startup, but its generic seed repair is **not** the implementation: lineage must never be healed to a fresh value. The owning call belongs to MC composition, not every GraphService importer. Preserve [MC's WAL availability tier](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/mcp/server/memory-core/Server.mjs#L456): a storage/readiness failure leaves publication/lineage unavailable; it must not turn graph readiness into a prerequisite for the ordinary WAL-local save path.

**Restore boundary — fence the mutation paths the product owns.** Lineage and family receipts share a graph snapshot; external private keys and issued envelopes do not roll back with it. [Disaster restore](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/scripts/maintenance/restore.mjs#L95) can replace the graph with an earlier bundle. [`DatabaseService.truncateDatabase`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/memory-core/DatabaseService.mjs#L839) and [`importGraphJsonl`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/memory-core/helpers/graphJsonlImport.mjs#L46) directly clear/insert graph rows, so ordinary GraphService write protection alone is insufficient.

The source leaf must cover supported graph import/replacement/truncation and target-set activation with a protected class-9 recovery fence admitted before their first relevant mutation and surviving their deletion/import transaction. Backup rows cannot clear it. Disposable staging is distinct from activation of a served plane. A crash after deletion must never restart as an unfenced empty lineage. Only the separately admitted recovery path may reconcile signer/trust/current publication state and clear the fence; ordinary setup/update cannot. The source-owner map and selected carrier follow; their crash/refusal cases are required implementation acceptance controls.

An out-of-band DB copy or volume snapshot is an administrative recovery operation requiring the same reconciliation. Equal heads do not certify that operation safe; no universal automatic rollback detection is claimed. Support for transparent undeclared restoration would reopen this boundary. This does not introduce a host-script step or credential question into normal setup/update.

**Selected fence carrier: one MC-owned operational table in the same SQLite database, outside `Nodes`/`Edges`.** It records a sticky class-9 recovery-required disposition bound to the plane and restoration operation/provenance. It contains neither family history nor signing secrets. Boot, the typed publication transaction and the family-admission snapshot reader read it directly; a missing/unreadable required fence state is unavailable, never a successful empty family map. No ordinary graph mutation, imported backup row, setup retry or configuration reservation clears it.

The lineage remains in the protected graph. Ada's optional relocation of the lineage into this table is **not selected**: the fence already prevents publication against restored lineage, while moving lineage would additionally change its backup/export contract. The operational table is justified because a fence node would change [exact graph population/fingerprint checks](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/memory-core/helpers/restoreTargetSetStorage.mjs#L773), and both row-replacement paths already leave other SQLite tables intact. This is one capability fence, not another family ledger.

| Supported owner | Fence admission boundary |
|---|---|
| `DatabaseService.truncateDatabase` and live replace import | Admit/preserve the fence in the same physical transaction as the first live delete; it survives the JSONL importer's subsequent `Nodes`/`Edges` delete/insert. The direct live-import arm must also be covered when no outer truncate ran. |
| Live **merge** import | Commit the fence before the first imported graph mutation; merge can insert absent protected records too. Import failure leaves the fence set. The trusted live owner supplies this policy, not a client-controlled “disposable” flag. |
| [`restoreTargetSetStorage.promoteGraph`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/services/memory-core/helpers/restoreTargetSetStorage.mjs#L639) | Admit/preserve it inside the live `.immediate()` transaction that deletes/copies rows. [Orchestrator](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/blob/533724f030aecf8a5b61e40e0374cbab0c8da17b/ai/daemons/orchestrator/Orchestrator.mjs#L835) passes the served GraphService connection. The later `promoted:graph` / `committed` ledger append is provenance, not the fence. |
| Receipt/edge restoration and legacy example | `restoreReceipts.mjs` must apply the live-merge fence or refuse protected edge types before bundle insertion. `ai/examples/db-restore-graph.mjs` must delegate to the fenced supported path or be explicitly retired/unsupported as administrative recovery. |
| Run-owned disposable target staging | No mutation of live eligibility. The staged bundle cannot carry authority to clear the live fence at promotion. |

The decisive activation control interrupts immediately after the promotion transaction commits but before its external `promoted:graph` receipt. Restart must remain fenced while restored rows are live. Also cover interrupted truncate, direct replace, merge, repeated imports, imported spoofed authority/fence data, unreadable fence state and publication racing the mutation. A common node-write guard or a post-commit status write fails these cases.

Clearing belongs to a separately admitted recovery operation after signer/trust/publication-state reconciliation; it is not an ordinary reservation mode or an “unfence” field in browser input. The source leaf must either implement and witness that authorized path or leave a named recovery-required refusal; it cannot claim automated recovery without the witness. That bound already applies to lost signer custody and does not change normal setup/update's no-extra-question outcome.

**Decision-record impact.** The proposed graduation amends ADR 0038 to record class-9 custody and boot/config authority; ADR 0041 gains the narrow post-plane reservation → original-host-run relation and pending-transition reconciliation. The per-run consent/effect record remains host-owned. The plane does not take over pre-plane bootstrap effects.

## Step-Back dispositions and acceptance obligations

Ada's Step-Back and subsequent C5/C6 reads support the publication carrier, L3 and reconciliation. C7 dispositions the last fence-carrier alternative and carries the additional live-promotion source finding into the controls. The contract carries the partial-point obligations in the contract:

1. **Authority:** this body is the candidate contract. Amend ADR 0038's ledger before implementation merge; retain ADR 0041/0006 and an ADR-0019-owned trust leaf. Record the class-9 ownership, storage, permitted verifier and non-alias rules explicitly.
2. **Consumers:** one complete immutable family snapshot feeds all readers. The publish gate (ADR 0042) is an explicit first consumer. Current `getCoreSwarmAgentFamilies` / `resolveReviewerFamily` derive from static roots; `publishExecutor` defaults its injected family resolver to null, and the default Fleet factory does not wire one. Retire the roots-only reader under Brain `#875`; do not deliver a writer whose new family the gate cannot see.
3. **Deterministic keys and durability:** name the MC receipt node-ID encoding for `(plane, stable issuer, operation id)`; use a domain-separated digest of a canonical tuple, not ambiguous concatenation. Fleet intent-path input includes the authenticated principal `owner:<connectionId>:<providerUserId>`, plane, seat and retry token. The intent/tombstone survives Fleet recreation and lives for the plane graph's lifetime. Host generation history must also remain selected across new setup/deploy run IDs; an empty current run is insufficient.
4. **Mutability/protection:** generalize the existing admitted-type guard, not a second bespoke guard. Cover reserved identities, labels, properties, edges, cold/warm rows, relabelling/deletion and decay; protect episode and receipt relationships. Test ordinary graph writers cannot manufacture authority. **Acknowledgment AC from Ada's final Step-Back:** census the raw-SQL identity migrations (`renameAgentIdentities`, `normalizeGraphIdentities`, `canonicalizeStoredAgentIdentities`, `reconcileRawMemoryGraphIdentities`, `migrateLegacyAdrIdentities`). A handle rename must not rewrite admitted family records; readers resolve former handles through the alias seam. Approved migration authority is not permission to silently mutate this record class.
5. **UX/retry:** a lost client token followed by a new click is a new operation, not an exactly-once continuation. Stale CAS must prevent a second effect, with read-back able to display “already applied” when appropriate. Do not promise browser-plus-shell restart recovery without client pending-act custody.
6. **Migration:** additive capability, unavailable until provisioned. First install, first update from an old verifier, normal update and recovery are separate witnesses. Source delivery does not imply installed acceptance.
7. **Active/archive:** episode history is authority; receipt is evidence; Fleet intent is dispatch custody. All survive their declared lifetime; retired host history must still participate in create-once decisions.
8. **Primitive reuse:** extract the pure canonicalizer into `ai/services/shared/` beside existing shared primitives, retaining/re-exporting its public path if needed. Strict closed typed input precedes canonicalization; do not expand its claims into general RFC-8785 compliance. Reuse exclusive lease/fsync atomic-write and secret-free descriptor patterns; class-9 provisioner is the only mint site, every use path is create-false.

Controls must falsify ordinary-seat and forged-principal publication, wrong purpose/audience/issuer/key, noncanonical/duplicate encodings, host-versus-plane authority, re-sign/idempotency, changed logical retries, stale revision, concurrent admissions, rollback and cold-row bypass. Include deliberate new-family/collision cases, null with its first producer, correction under transfer, receipt/edge decay, full snapshot completeness, process recreation and storage-unavailable reads.

Provisioning controls must interrupt before mint, after durable attempt, after stage, before consumption and after consumption; exercise changed input, failed receipt, new run ID, retired history, lost history/custody and wrong-target observations. The pre-class-9 verifier must remain unknown until a supported witness is available. Test both update phases, failure between them, stale locks and final readiness; do not count an intermediate deployment receipt as publication capability.

## Convergence dispositions and graduation criteria

| Alternative / live falsifier | Disposition | Residual / required control |
|---|---|---|
| A1 dedicated HTTP publication | Adopt in proposed convergence. AuthService owns policy after common guards; Transport remains transport. | Exact supported auth-profile/route controls; no provisioned silent bypass. |
| A2 class-9-on-MCP | Not selected for this slice. It is viable but adds service-context/list/call/session policy to the same trust bootstrap. | Reopen if the complete MCP carrier becomes smaller or another consumer requires it. |
| B signed operation with ordinary MCP auth | Not selected; it does not remove distinct service authority and introduces a transport-credential dependency. | Never substitute a viewer/seat credential for Fleet publication. |
| C MC write with fresh Fleet ownership pull | Not selected; no admitted ownership projection exists and this adds a reverse dependency. | Reopen on a separately admitted ownership carrier; the correction distinguishing write-time authorization from read-time freshness stands. |
| L1 host-only cross-run index | Not selected for automatic continuation. Missing host history must refuse, and the plane can supply the shared attempt index without another generic host ledger. | A moved/reprovisioned host may still require recovery when its original attempt record is absent. |
| L2 provisioner mutation API | Not selected; its privilege is not supplied by existing PAT authentication. | Would require an explicit server-side authority/credential-reuse contract. |
| L3 boot-config-owned plane reservation | Adopt in proposed convergence. It reuses configuration authority, with original-run linkage and split reserve/generate effects. | All interruption, lost-acknowledgement, changed-input and conflicting-descriptor controls above. |
| Fingerprint before generation | Rejected as impossible. Reserve identifiers first; bind derived fingerprint after durable key creation. | No caller-supplied future fingerprint establishes a key. |
| Empty current run / absent consumption proves virgin custody | Rejected. Read the plane reservation and original attempt's retained history. | New-run, changed-root, lost-record and staged-key-loss negatives. |
| Head comparison diagnoses all rollback | Rejected. Matching pending target reconciles normally; equal rewound domains are indistinguishable. | No universal anti-rollback claim; supported mutation owners fence, out-of-band restoration is administrative recovery. |
| Fence in graph nodes vs operational table | Choose the separate operational table. It survives row replacement without changing graph fingerprints. | Same-transaction live mutation fencing, direct read at publication/snapshot, no imported clear. |
| Move lineage into the fence table | Not selected. Not needed for the fence, and would change lineage backup/export semantics. | Lineage stays protected graph state; restoration remains fenced until recovery reconciliation. |

The byte-profile precedent check includes [HTTP Message Signatures / RFC 9421](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9421) and [JWS / RFC 7515](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7515), outside the current peer discussion. The former signs selected HTTP components; the latter provides an object-signature serialization. The named Neo fixed-purpose profile deliberately retains the existing two-segment Ed25519 pattern with separate custody/domain binding; neither standards-compliance label is claimed. A general-purpose external interchange requirement would reopen that profile decision.

**OQ1–OQ4:** the chosen carrier, delivered plane admission, boot reservation/update/restore contract and physical admission/snapshot boundaries are now concrete proposed dispositions above. Their C7 implementations remain acceptance work, not source facts; C8's membership extension has its own quorum and real delivery artifacts above and below. **OQ5 remains the policy decision:** authorization at issuance, exact five-minute delivery, one shared wall clock; every re-sign reauthorizes. Ordinary detach/transfer tolerates that window and CAS orders confirmations. Revalidate for automatic/adversarial transfer, longer validity or different issuer/verifier clocks. A stricter future profile can use Fleet-local delivery leases/drain; no cross-service revocation protocol is assumed necessary.

Version-bound GPT/Claude quorum and the final Step-Back delta are recorded below; Ada expressly extends her approval to the two census-AC tightenings. The decision-record artifacts are [Institution #816 / PR #817](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/pull/817) and [Brain #1294 / PR #1295](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/pull/1295). Their acceptance requires review and human merge. The source/UI artifact mapping below is complete; graduation does not certify source or installed delivery.

## Delivery map

The [#700 author's disposition](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/discussions/811#discussioncomment-19190367) keeps the existing outcome as the manual-v1 parent. These four source/UI leaves are native children; Sophie owns their delivery and integration.

| Artifact | Owned acceptance |
|---|---|
| [Brain #1296](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/1296) | MC typed admission, boot reservation/trust, protected membership/declaration history and restore fence, complete temporal projection and all named readers |
| [Brain #1297](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/1297) | Fleet durable membership/manual-act outbox, operator methods, signer and existing provisioner custody/update integration, authenticated binding projection |
| [Brain #1298](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/1298) | Host usability at Start/final spawn/restart/grant/recovery/redemption and exact completed-removal outcome |
| [Institution #819](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/819) | Explicit Detail confirmation/correction, bound retry/readback and C8's five named states/remedies; related to Brain #875, without copying Brain #28's participation authority |

Decision-record prerequisites remain separate: [Institution #816 / PR #817](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/pull/817) supplies C7 ADR0038; [Brain #1294 / PR #1295](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/pull/1295) supplies ADR0041's original-run relation; [Institution #818](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/818) supplies the C8 ADR0038 follow-up and depends on #816. Implementation merges require the accepted records.

Native blockers verified 2026-10-26T08:36Z: #1296 depends on Institution #818 and Brain #1294; #1297 on #1296; #1298 on #1297; Institution #819 on Brain #1298. The chain retains all source prerequisites without duplicate outcome tickets.

[Brain #1299](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/1299) preserves the earlier declared-model/Start/bound-read-back contract as a standalone post-v1 ticket, blocked by #700 and **not** its child. Institution #414 remains blocked by #700 and owns the joined installed witness. The parent body/label conversion stays with Grace; the concrete children and dependency edges are already present. Source validation cannot close the installed witness.

**Implementation-policy disposition:** Grace has resolved the multiple-seat policy in Brain #700's ledger. Its complete-membership transport and ordering are the separately graduated C8 contract above; C7's earlier signals do not cover that delta.

## Signal Ledger

- **gpt:** [AUTHOR_SIGNAL by @neo-gpt-sophie @ body updatedAt 2026-10-26T04:12:12Z], [comment 19188256](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/discussions/811#discussioncomment-19188256).
- **claude:** [GRADUATION_APPROVED by @neo-opus-ada @ body updatedAt 2026-10-26T04:12:12Z], [comment 19188284](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/discussions/811#discussioncomment-19188284). The signal explicitly extends to this sole tightening: the receipt/example restore census and immutable-family-record identity-migration ACs above.
- **gemini:** no graduation signal requested or received for this protocol; no coverage/consent claimed.

The author accepts the two acknowledgment ACs. Those are the only contract changes after the C7 signal anchor; Ada explicitly extends her signal to that tightening. Earlier design contributions are not relabelled as approval.

## Unresolved Dissent

No formal graduation DEFERRED/VETO signal is asserted. All pre-fold options and falsifiers have explicit dispositions above; peers may reopen a substantive delta during the final read.

## Unresolved Liveness

Clio's combined Monday read remains on her lane; no response is inferred from silence. No absent family is counted as assent. This changes a service protocol, not a core value, critical gate or consensus rule. Live routing at 04:08Z showed Sophie/gpt and Ada/claude active; family quorum still requires their actual bound signals, not presence.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

- Manual authority and no silent credential alias → exact route, envelope, operator/seat, class-9 custody and negative-authority controls.
- Stable first-install/update/retry identity → L3 reservation, original-run relation, split effects, explicit-null first producer and re-sign/CAS controls.
- Complete admitted-state readers and integrity → physical transaction, protection/decay, immutable snapshot and all consumers including publication gate.
- Recovery safety without fictitious detection → operational fence at live import/truncate/promotion, interruption controls, explicit recovery boundary.
- Product acceptance → the four manual-v1 children of Brain `#700` join Institution `#414`'s installed Add/ownership/confirmation witness; post-v1 automatic Start/read-back is Brain `#1299`.

Related: neomjs/neo-agent-brain#700

nodes.title: Agent Registry - Proposal
nodes.body: Hi, There are a few open discussions related to agent registry to enable agent discovery discussed [here](https://google-a2a.github.io/A2A/latest/topics/agent-discovery/#2-curated-registries-catalog-based-discovery). The following is a proposal for a registry service for agents. We appreciate any feedback or discussions in solidifying the proposal. --- # Agent Registry \- Proposal With the rapid proliferation of AI and Agentic applications, a typical enterprise may have a number of internally developed agentic applications and agents procured from external vendors hosted internally or in the cloud. An enterprise customer may have functions that span more than one agent and need a service to lookup and leverage the available agents for completing a task. Similarly, vendors may also provide a number of agents as part of their offerings similar to how public APIs are documented today. The vendors of agents may need to provide a list of available agents for consumption to their customers. These agents could be publicly accessible or granted by entitlements to their customers. This paper proposes a registry service that could be deployed to enterprise environments or publicly accessible endpoints that can help with agent discovery and entitlements. The following are the key terms used in this document: ***Agents:*** Agentic applications running within an enterprise or hosted externally. ***Agent Card:*** A JSON document published by an agent describing its capabilities, protocols and authentication mechanisms. ***Client***: A client is an application, service or an agent that can consume Agents ***Agent Entitlement:*** A permission granted to a client to enable fetching available agents for its use. ## Agent Catalog Agent Catalog is a component of the Agent Registry that allows showing a list of available agents in an enterprise context. The registry service allows authenticated users to login using a web interface and add agents hosted internally or externally to the catalog. Agents can be added to the catalog by providing their Agent Card url which describes the agent’s capabilities, skills and supported authentication schemes. Registry will fetch the content from the provided agent card and index the content to offer search capabilities. Following is an example mockup showing a list of available agents in an enterprise agent catalog: Agents added to the catalog can have varying capabilities, authentication mechanisms and supported protocols. But the catalog’s role is to simply surface the details of an agent and does not deal with the internal workings of an agent. Enterprise administrators can choose to make the agents available publicly or set them up to be available only for authenticated clients. ## Agent Entitlements Agents available in the registry can be entitled to client applications. A client application can be a service, application or even an agent. The registry service provides an interface for logged in users to register a new client and allow the client to access the available agent entitlements. The agent registry could leverage an external authorization server for generating the client\_id and client\_secret and use the OAuth 2.0 Client Credential grant flow to request an access\_token and use the token to access the entitlement service. A registered client can issue HTTP GET to https://\/agents/entitled with the bearer token to retrieve a list of entitled agents represented by their agent cards. Following is an example response: ```json { "registry_version": "0.1", "resources": [ { "id": "it-agent", "name": "IT Agent", "location": { "url": "https://it.example.com/.well-known/agent.json", "type": "agent_card" }, }, { "id": "benefits-agent", "name": "Benefits Agent", "location": { "url": "https://benefits.example.com/it/agent.json", "type": "agent_card" } } ], "total_count": 2 } ``` The entitlements provide links to the agent cards published by the agent providers. ## Open Discovery Enterprises may choose to provide a public listing of available agents that could be used by external agents/applications or to be discovered by search engines. For example, an agent vendor may provide a publicly accessible list of agents that could be accessed by any other external clients. We propose to use ***https://\/agents/public*** as the endpoint for open discovery of agents published by an enterprise. ## Agent Search Agent registry can support agent search for consumers. A client application can query the registry with a query \+ filter criteria to discover agents (entitled/public agents) on the fly for solving a task. For example: if a consumer queries “what’s the 401k match policy?”, the registry can perform a search of all the available entitled agents for that consumer and can return the most relevant agents (e.g. Benefits Agent) to the consumer. Clients can pass top as a query parameter to limit the results returned by the registry. Specifying top=1 query parameter returns the top 1 match for the query. A search can be performed by HTTP POST to https://\/agents/search with payload ```json { "query":"", "capabilities": { "streaming": true, "pushNotifications": true } } ``` ## End to end flow: Following diagram demonstrates the end-to-end flow between the services: ## High level diagram ## User authentication and authorization to registry User management will be available as part of the Agent registry service and agent registries can leverage Single Sign-On with an external IdP for enterprise authentication and authorization. Users can be assigned one or more of the following roles: ***Administrator*** \- Ability to setup auth configuration, settings and user management ***Catalog Manager*** \- Ability to add or remove agents to the catalog ***User*** \- Ability to register new clients and grant agent entitlements ***Viewer*** \- Ability to view the agent catalog if the catalog is not publicly accessible ## Agent registry end points: 1. **Open Discovery end point:** GET URL: https://\/agents/public Any agents added to the registry and configured with public access will be listed at this endpoint. 2. **Agent entitlements end point** GET URL: https://\/agents/entitled All public \+ entitled agents available for a client will be returned by this endpoint. 3. **Search end point** POST URL: https://\/agents/search Client’s accessible public \+ entitled agents that match the provided search criteria will be returned via this endpoint. Endpoints # 2 and # 3 are accessible only for authenticated clients. Pagination is supported by passing ***top*** and ***skip*** query parameters.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-04-10 ### Added - PostgresFs: full `IFileSystem` implementation backed by PostgreSQL (`vfs_files` table). - 75+ bash commands via just-bash with the custom Postgres filesystem backend. - Three-tier hybrid search: full-text (tsvector), fuzzy/regex (pg_trgm), and optional semantic similarity (pgvector). - Auto-embedding pipeline: files embedded on write when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set; graceful degradation without it. - Multi-tenant isolation via `tenant_id` column and Row-Level Security. - bash-tool adapter: `createPostgresVfsTool()` factory for drop-in Vercel AI SDK integration. - Custom shell commands: `search`, `tag`, `untag`, `tags`, `recent`, `summarize`. - Web UI: three-column file manager with tenant selector, markdown preview, hybrid search, drag-and-drop, and responsive layout. - REST API for programmatic file operations. - In-memory caching of path tree, directory listings, and stat data. - Four runnable demo scripts under `examples/` with swappable seed data. - Database migration runner (`bun run migrate`). nodes.title: Plan: OPA-Based Row Filtering & Column Masking in QueryFlux
nodes.body:
# Plan: OPA-Based Row Filtering & Column Masking in QueryFlux

## Context

QueryFlux proxies queries across multiple engines (Trino, DuckDB, StarRocks, Athena, etc.) but currently has no data-level access control — once a user passes cluster-group authorization (OpenFGA/SimplePolicy), they see all data. This plan adds **row filtering** and **column masking** enforced at the proxy layer, before SQL reaches any backend engine, using OPA as the external policy engine. This gives uniform enforcement across all engines without touching any of them.

Key distinction from Trino's native OPA plugin: Trino hands OPA expressions to its internal query planner which handles AST injection. QueryFlux has no query planner — it must rewrite SQL itself using sqlglot.

---

## Architecture Diagram

```
Client (Trino/PG/MySQL/FlightSQL)
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   QueryFlux Proxy                   │
│                                                     │
│  [Frontend Protocol Handler]                        │
│         │ IncomingQuery {sql, session}              │
│         ▼                                           │
│  [AuthProvider] → AuthContext {user, groups, roles} │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼                                           │
│  [Router] → ClusterGroupName                        │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼                                           │
│  [AuthorizationChecker / OpenFGA] ── cluster gate   │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼                                           │
│  [TranslationService / sqlglot] ── dialect rewrite  │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼  ◄── NEW ──────────────────────────────  │
│  [SQL Table + Column Extractor]                     │
│    sqlglot.parse_one + qualify pass                 │
│    → list of (catalog, schema, table, columns)      │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼  ◄── NEW ──────────────────────────────  │
│  [OpaClient]                                        │
│    POST GetRowFilters per table                     │
│    POST GetColumnMask per column (or batch)         │
│    → row_filters[] + column_masks[]                 │
│         │                                           │
│         ▼  ◄── NEW ──────────────────────────────  │
│  [SQL Rewriter]                                     │
│    qualify pass → resolve a.email → users.email     │
│    inject WHERE predicates per table                │
│    replace column refs with mask expressions        │
│    expand SELECT * via CatalogProvider              │
│    transpile mask expressions to target dialect     │
│         │ rewritten SQL                             │
│         ▼                                           │
│  [Engine Adapter]                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         │
         ├──► Trino        ← same rewritten SQL
         ├──► DuckDB       ← mask expressions transpiled to DuckDB dialect
         ├──► StarRocks     ← mask expressions transpiled to StarRocks dialect
         └──► Athena        ← mask expressions transpiled to Athena dialect

         ▲
         │  OPA policy bundle (Rego)
┌────────┴──────────┐
│   OPA Server      │  external, shared, policy-as-code
│                   │  same bundle can serve Trino native OPA too
└───────────────────┘
```

---

## Context Properties: Passing Runtime Values to OPA

Clients can pass arbitrary key/value context to OPA via **session params** — a separate channel from tags, so they never reach Prometheus or the admin panel. This is the designed pattern for microservices that need to scope queries at runtime (e.g. `customer_id`, `tenant_id`).

### How clients set session params

| Protocol | How to set | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Trino HTTP | `X-Trino-Session: customer_id=123` header | Per-request (each POST /v1/statement) |
| Postgres | `SET SESSION customer_id = '123'` | Per-connection (microservice resets before each query) |
| MySQL | `SET SESSION customer_id = '123'` | Per-connection |

These land in `SessionContext.session_params` (currently parsed but not forwarded anywhere). QueryFlux forwards the entire `session_params` map to OPA as `context.properties`.

### Why not query tags?

Tags (`X-Trino-Client-Tags`, `SET query_tags`) already flow to Prometheus metrics and the admin panel. Using them for runtime context like `customer_id` would pollute metric label cardinality. Session params are structurally separate and never reach metrics — no whitelist or filtering config needed.

### OPA receives session params as properties

```json
{
  "input": {
    "context": {
      "identity": { "user": "alice", "groups": ["analysts"] },
      "properties": {
        "customer_id": "123",
        "tenant_id": "acme-corp"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Rego uses them to build dynamic expressions:

```rego
row_filters[filter] {
  input.action.operation == "GetRowFilters"
  input.action.resource.table.tableName == "orders"
  customer_id := input.context.properties["customer_id"]
  filter := { "expression": sprintf("customer_id = '%s'", [customer_id]) }
}
```

### Microservice flow

```
microservice receives: GET /api/orders?customer_id=123
        ↓
Trino client sends to QueryFlux:
  POST /v1/statement
  X-Trino-Session: customer_id=123
  Body: SELECT * FROM orders
        ↓
QueryFlux → OPA: properties: { customer_id: "123" }
        ↓
Rego builds: "customer_id = '123'"
        ↓
SQL rewritten: WHERE ... AND customer_id = '123'
```

---

## OPA Schema (aligned with Trino's native OPA plugin)

Aligning with Trino's schema means a single Rego bundle can serve both Trino (for users who also have Trino's native OPA plugin) and QueryFlux for all other engines.

### Row Filters Request (per table)
```json
POST /v1/data/queryflux/row_filters
{
  "input": {
    "context": {
      "identity": { "user": "alice", "groups": ["analysts", "eu-team"], "roles": ["reader"] },
      "properties": { "customer_id": "123" },
      "queryfluxVersion": "0.2.0"
    },
    "action": {
      "operation": "GetRowFilters",
      "resource": {
        "table": { "catalogName": "hive", "schemaName": "prod", "tableName": "users" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Row Filters Response
```json
{
  "result": [
    { "expression": "region = 'EU'" },
    { "expression": "status = 'active'" }
  ]
}
```
Multiple expressions are ANDed together.

### Column Mask Request (per column, or batch)
```json
POST /v1/data/queryflux/column_mask
{
  "input": {
    "context": {
      "identity": { "user": "alice", "groups": ["analysts"] }
    },
    "action": {
      "operation": "GetColumnMask",
      "resource": {
        "column": {
          "catalogName": "hive", "schemaName": "prod", "tableName": "users",
          "columnName": "email", "columnType": "varchar"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Column Mask Response
```json
{ "result": { "expression": "SHA2(email, 256)" } }
// or null — no mask
{ "result": null }
```

### Example Rego
```rego
package queryflux

row_filters[filter] {
  input.action.operation == "GetRowFilters"
  input.action.resource.table.tableName == "users"
  "analysts" in input.context.identity.groups
  filter := { "expression": "region = 'EU'" }
}

column_masks := mask {
  input.action.operation == "GetColumnMask"
  input.action.resource.column.columnName == "ssn"
  not "hr" in input.context.identity.groups
  mask := { "expression": "NULL" }
}
```

---

## SQL Rewriting — Step by Step

### Step 1: Parse + Qualify
```python
import sqlglot
from sqlglot.optimizer import qualify

ast = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, dialect=src_dialect)
# qualify resolves all column refs to table-qualified form
# requires schema_dict: { "users": { "email": "VARCHAR", "ssn": "VARCHAR", ... } }
ast = qualify.qualify(ast, schema=schema_dict, dialect=src_dialect)
# now: a.email is internally stored as users.email
```

Schema dict comes from `CatalogProvider::get_table_schema()`. Required (not optional) when masked tables are present.

### Step 2: Row Filter Injection
```python
# For each table with a filter, walk AST and inject into WHERE at every scan node
for node in ast.walk():
    if isinstance(node, exp.From) and references_table(node, "users"):
        inject_where(node.parent_select, "region = 'EU' AND status = 'active'")
```

### Step 3: Column Mask Rewriting
```python
# masks = { "email": "SHA2({col}, 256)", "ssn": "NULL" }
for node in ast.walk():
    if isinstance(node, exp.Select):
        for col in node.expressions:
            table, name = resolve_column(col)  # uses qualify result
            if (table, name) in masks:
                expr_str = masks[(table, name)].replace("{col}", col.sql())
                node.set(col, sqlglot.parse_one(f"{expr_str} AS {name}"))
```

Note: `{col}` in the expression is substituted with the actual qualified column reference (`a.email`), so the expression becomes `SHA2(a.email, 256) AS email`.

### Step 4: SELECT * Expansion
```python
if is_star_select(ast) and table_has_masks(table):
    columns = catalog_provider.get_table_schema(catalog, schema, table).columns
    # expand * to explicit columns, then apply Step 3
```

If schema unavailable → reject query with: `"SELECT * is not permitted on masked table hive.prod.users; use explicit columns"`

### Step 5: Transpile Mask Expressions to Target Dialect
OPA policy authors write expressions in one canonical dialect (Trino/ANSI). Before injection, each expression is transpiled to the target engine dialect via the existing sqlglot pipeline:
```python
# expr from OPA: "SHA2(email, 256)" (written in Trino dialect)
expr_transpiled = sqlglot.transpile(expr, read="trino", write=target_dialect)[0]
# DuckDB → "sha256(email)"
# StarRocks → "SHA2(email, 256)"  (unchanged, already compatible)
```
Same behavior as main query translation — unknown functions pass through unchanged.

---

## New Crate: `queryflux-access-control`

```
crates/queryflux-access-control/
  src/
    lib.rs          # AccessControlService trait + factory fn
    opa_client.rs   # HTTP client: POST OPA endpoints, token caching
    extractor.rs    # Extract (catalog, schema, table, columns) from SQL via sqlglot/PyO3
    rewriter.rs     # qualify → inject WHERE → mask columns → expand SELECT *
    model.rs        # OpaInput, OpaOutput, RowFilter, ColumnMask, TableRef, EnforcedQuery
    noop.rs         # No-op impl (when accessControl.provider = none)
```

### Service Trait
```rust
#[async_trait]
pub trait AccessControlService: Send + Sync {
    async fn enforce(
        &self,
        sql: &str,
        auth_ctx: &AuthContext,
        session: &SessionContext,          // carries session_params → OPA context.properties
        group: &ClusterGroupName,
        protocol: &FrontendProtocol,
        src_dialect: &SqlDialect,
        tgt_dialect: &SqlDialect,
        catalog_provider: &Arc<dyn CatalogProvider>,
    ) -> Result<EnforcedQuery>;
}

pub struct EnforcedQuery {
    pub sql: String,
    pub row_filters_applied: Vec<String>,   // policy expressions, for audit
    pub columns_masked: Vec<String>,         // column names, for audit
}
```

### OPA Client (mirrors OpenFgaAuthorizationClient pattern)
```rust
pub struct OpaClient {
    config: OpaConfig,
    http_client: reqwest::Client,                                    // reuse workspace reqwest
    token_cache: tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<(String, Instant)>>,     // same pattern as OpenFGA client
}
```
- Token caching: copy pattern from `queryflux-auth/src/authorization.rs:135-182`
- `fail_behavior: deny` → return `Err` if OPA unreachable (query rejected)
- `fail_behavior: allow` → return original SQL unchanged if OPA unreachable

---

## Config (in `queryflux-core/src/config.rs`)

```yaml
accessControl:
  provider: opa           # or "none" (default)
  opa:
    rowFiltersUri: http://opa:8181/v1/data/queryflux/row_filters
    columnMaskUri: http://opa:8181/v1/data/queryflux/column_mask
    # optional batch endpoint for column masks (fewer HTTP round trips)
    batchColumnMaskUri: http://opa:8181/v1/data/queryflux/batch_column_mask
    timeoutMs: 100
    failBehavior: deny    # or "allow"
    # expression dialect: dialect OPA policy authors write mask expressions in
    # QueryFlux transpiles from this to the target engine dialect
    expressionDialect: trino
    credentials:          # optional, same shape as OpenFgaCredentials
      method: client_credentials
      clientId: queryflux
      clientSecret: secret
      tokenEndpoint: https://keycloak/token
```

### Rust structs
```rust
pub struct AccessControlConfig {
    pub provider: AccessControlProviderConfig,  // None | Opa
    pub opa: Option<OpaConfig>,
}

pub struct OpaConfig {
    pub row_filters_uri: String,
    pub column_mask_uri: String,
    pub batch_column_mask_uri: Option<String>,
    pub timeout_ms: u64,
    pub fail_behavior: FailBehavior,
    pub expression_dialect: SqlDialect,   // dialect mask expressions are written in
    pub credentials: Option<OpaCredentials>,
}
```

---

## Integration in `dispatch.rs`

Single injection point for **both** async and sync paths, between translation and adapter submission.

### Async path (`dispatch_query`, after line 191)
```rust
let sql = state.translation.maybe_translate(&sql, &src, &tgt, ...).await?;

// NEW
let catalog_provider = { state.live.read().await.catalog_provider.clone() };
let enforced = state.access_control
    .enforce(&sql, auth_ctx, &group, &protocol, &src, &tgt, &catalog_provider)
    .await?;
let sql = enforced.sql;
// enforced metadata stored in QueryContext for audit

let execution = adapter.submit_query(&sql, &session, &credentials, &tags).await?;
```

### Sync path (`execute_stream`, before line 791)
Same pattern — `enforce()` applied to `setup.translated` before `adapter.execute_as_arrow()`.

---

## Files to Create / Modify

| Action | File | Change |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Create** | `crates/queryflux-access-control/` | New crate |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux-core/src/config.rs` | Add `AccessControlConfig`, `OpaConfig`; add `access_control` to `ProxyConfig` |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux-frontend/src/state.rs` | Add `access_control: Arc<dyn AccessControlService>` to `AppState` |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux-frontend/src/dispatch.rs` | Inject `enforce()` in `dispatch_query()` (~line 191) and `execute_stream()` (~line 791) |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux-frontend/src/admin.rs` | Add dry-run: `GET /admin/access-control/effective?user=&table=` |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux-persistence/src/metrics_store.rs` | Add `row_filters_applied` and `columns_masked` to `QueryRecord` |
| **Modify** | `crates/queryflux/src/main.rs` | Instantiate `AccessControlService` before AppState construction (~line 728) |
| **Modify** | `Cargo.toml` (workspace) | Add `queryflux-access-control` to workspace members |

### Reuse (do not reimplement)
- `reqwest::Client` — HTTP calls to OPA (same as `TrinoAdapter`, `OpenFgaAuthorizationClient`)
- Token cache pattern — `tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<(String, Instant)>>` from `authorization.rs:119-182`
- PyO3 `spawn_blocking` + `Python::attach` + `PyDict` pattern — from `sqlglot.rs:53-96`
- `CatalogProvider::get_table_schema()` — already in `queryflux-core/src/catalog.rs`
- `sqlglot.parse_one` + `qualify.qualify` — already available via existing PyO3 bridge
- `sqlglot.transpile` — for mask expression dialect conversion

---

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1 — Foundation (no behavior change)
- [ ] Create `queryflux-access-control` crate with `NoopAccessControlService`
- [ ] Add `AccessControlConfig` + `OpaConfig` to `queryflux-core/src/config.rs`
- [ ] Add `access_control` to `AppState`, wire noop in `main.rs`
- [ ] Inject passthrough `enforce()` call in both `dispatch.rs` paths

### Phase 2 — OPA Client + Table/Column Extractor
- [ ] Implement `OpaClient` (reqwest POST, token cache, fail_behavior, timeout)
- [ ] Implement `extract_tables_and_columns()` via `sqlglot.parse_one` + AST walk (PyO3, spawn_blocking)
- [ ] Unit tests: CTEs, JOINs, subqueries, UNION, aliased tables

### Phase 3 — SQL Rewriter
- [ ] `qualify` pass integration (requires schema from `CatalogProvider`)
- [ ] Row filter injection (WHERE append + AST walker for CTEs/subqueries)
- [ ] Column mask rewriting for explicit column lists
- [ ] `SELECT *` expansion + masking; reject with clear error if schema unavailable
- [ ] Mask expression transpilation to target dialect via sqlglot
- [ ] Integration tests: Trino and DuckDB backends

### Phase 4 — Audit + Admin
- [ ] Add `row_filters_applied` / `columns_masked` to `QueryRecord`
- [ ] Propagate `EnforcedQuery` metadata through `QueryContext` to `record_query()`
- [ ] Admin dry-run endpoint: `GET /admin/access-control/effective?user=&table=`

### Phase 5 — Hardening
- [ ] OPA response caching (short TTL, keyed on `(user, groups_hash, table_ref)`)
- [ ] Batch column mask endpoint support (fewer HTTP round trips)
- [ ] Config validation: error if `provider: opa` but `opa:` block missing
- [ ] Example Rego policies + documentation

---

## Verification

1. **Unit**: `cargo test -p queryflux-access-control` — table extraction, SQL rewriting, OPA client (mock server)
2. **Integration**: Start OPA with example Rego bundle; configure QueryFlux with `accessControl.provider: opa`; issue queries as user in `analysts` group:
   - Row filter: query returns only rows matching filter
   - Column mask: `ssn` → `NULL`, `email` → hashed value
   - `QueryRecord.columns_masked` and `row_filters_applied` logged correctly
3. **Cross-engine**: Same Rego policy applied to queries routed to both Trino and DuckDB groups; mask expressions correctly transpiled per engine
4. **Fail behavior**: Stop OPA; `failBehavior: deny` rejects queries; `failBehavior: allow` passes through unchanged
5. **Dry-run**: `GET /admin/access-control/effective?user=alice&table=hive.prod.users` returns expected filters and masks

---

## Open Issues (for discussion)

### 1. Column qualification in mask expressions (`a.email` problem)
OPA returns `"SHA2(email, 256)"` where `email` is a bare column name. When the query uses a table alias (`SELECT a.email FROM users a JOIN ...`), the rewriter must substitute the correct qualified reference (`a.email`) into the expression, producing `SHA2(a.email, 256)`.

This requires:
- sqlglot `qualify` pass to resolve all column refs before injection (needs schema from `CatalogProvider`)
- The rewriter to find the qualified alias for each masked column and substitute it into the expression string

**Discussion**: Does this make `CatalogProvider` a hard requirement for all masked tables? What's the fallback if schema is unavailable — reject the query or apply the mask with bare column name and risk SQL errors?

---

### 2. Mask expression dialect portability
OPA policy authors write expressions like `SHA2(email, 256)` in one dialect (e.g. Trino). When QueryFlux routes to DuckDB (`sha256(email)`) or StarRocks, the expression must be transpiled.

Current proposal: run mask expressions through `sqlglot.transpile(expr, read=expressionDialect, write=tgt_dialect)`. sqlglot covers many function equivalences but not all. Unknown functions pass through unchanged — which may silently produce invalid SQL on the target engine.

**Discussion**: Is silent pass-through acceptable? Should we validate that the transpiled expression is parseable in the target dialect and error if not? Or should we document that policy authors must test expressions per engine?

---

### 3. SELECT * on masked tables
When a query uses `SELECT *` on a table with column masks, QueryFlux must expand `*` to explicit column names before applying masks. This requires knowing the full column list from `CatalogProvider`.

**Discussion**: What if the catalog provider isn't configured or doesn't have the schema? Options:
- **Reject** the query with a clear error (safe but may break existing queries)
- **Pass through** without masking (unsafe — leaks data)
- **Apply masks at result batch level** (`ResultSink.on_batch()`) as fallback — catches it post-execution but backend still processed unmasked data

---

### 4. OPA call per table/column vs single batched call
Trino calls OPA once per table (row filters) and once per column (column masks), potentially many HTTP round trips for wide tables. Trino also has a batch column mask endpoint.

**Discussion**: Should QueryFlux make one OPA call per query (sending all tables + columns in one request) vs following Trino's per-table/per-column model? One call is simpler and faster; per-table/per-column aligns with Trino's schema and enables sharing Rego policies between Trino and QueryFlux.

---

### 5. CTE and subquery rewriting correctness
Row filters and column masks must be applied at every scan node of a filtered table — including inside CTEs, derived tables, UNION branches, and subqueries. sqlglot's AST walker can reach all of these, but complex queries (correlated subqueries, lateral joins, recursive CTEs) may have edge cases.

**Discussion**: Should we start with a limited scope (top-level FROM only, no CTEs/subqueries) and expand iteratively? Or handle the full AST from the start and accept that edge cases may surface in production?

---

### 6. `identity` field in OPA response (security context)
Trino's OPA schema supports an optional `identity` field in each `ViewExpression` — this specifies which user's security context the mask/filter expression should be evaluated under (e.g., a service account with broader access). Trino's query planner handles this natively.

QueryFlux has no equivalent mechanism. If OPA returns an `identity` field, QueryFlux would ignore it.

**Discussion**: Is the `identity` field needed for our use cases? If so, how would QueryFlux honor it — run the expression as a different user? This may be out of scope for v1.

---

### 7. Performance impact of qualify pass
The sqlglot `qualify` pass (needed to resolve `a.email` → `users.email`) requires schema information and is more expensive than dialect-only transpilation. It also currently isn't used in the main translation path (dispatch.rs passes empty `SchemaContext`).

**Discussion**: Is the latency acceptable? Should we only run qualify when masked tables are present in the query (lazy activation)? What's the expected p99 latency of `qualify` + OPA call + rewrite vs. current translation-only path?

---

### 8. Interaction with SQL translation (ordering)
Currently the plan applies access control **after** dialect translation. This means OPA Rego and mask expressions are written against the **source dialect** SQL (as the client wrote it), and mask expressions are then transpiled to the target dialect.

Alternative: apply access control **before** translation, against the original client SQL. Simpler for OPA (no translated SQL surprises), but mask expressions would need to be in source dialect and may not match the translated table/column names (if translation renames anything).

**Discussion**: Which ordering is correct — pre or post translation? Are there cases in QueryFlux where translation renames tables or columns (not just function syntax)?

---

### 9. Session param injection (SQL injection risk)
Client-supplied session params (e.g. `customer_id=123`) are forwarded to OPA and Rego uses them to build SQL expressions via `sprintf`. A malicious client could send `customer_id = "1' OR '1'='1"` producing invalid or dangerous SQL.

OPA returns a finished SQL string — QueryFlux injects it verbatim. There is no parameterization layer between OPA's `sprintf` output and the SQL sent to the backend.

**Discussion**: Should QueryFlux sanitize session param values before forwarding to OPA (e.g. reject values containing quotes or SQL keywords)? Or is this the Rego policy author's responsibility to validate? Should there be a `trustedSessionParams` allowlist in config so only explicitly named params are forwarded to OPA?

---

### 10. Session param scope for Postgres/MySQL connections
For Postgres and MySQL, `SET SESSION customer_id = '123'` is connection-scoped. A microservice reusing a pooled connection must re-issue the SET before each query, adding a round trip. If it forgets, a previous request's `customer_id` bleeds into the next.

For Trino HTTP, `X-Trino-Session` is per-request (each POST /v1/statement), so this is not a problem.

**Discussion**: Should QueryFlux warn or error if masked tables are queried over Postgres/MySQL without any session params set? Or is this purely an application-level concern?

nodes.title: AI-SPM v1.0.0 — AI Security Posture Management
nodes.body:
# AI-SPM v1.0.0 — AI Security Posture Management **Release date:** 2026-04-25 **Codename:** "MCP" > First production release of the AI Security Posture Management. Customers > can now upload their own AI agents as a single Python file, deploy > them into sandboxed containers, and have them chat through the full > security pipeline — prompt-guard → policy decider → Kafka → output-guard > — with attached policies, conversation memory, web search, and a live > activity timeline visible in the admin UI. --- ## Highlights - **End-to-end agent chat** through the existing AI-SPM security pipeline, with attached per-agent policies enforced on every turn. - **Drop-in agent uploads.** Operator drops in a single `agent.py`, the platform validates it, mints per-agent tokens, spawns a sandboxed Docker container, and routes traffic through Kafka. No custom image required for the five example agent shapes we ship. - **Provider-agnostic LLM proxy.** Native dispatch for Anthropic and Ollama (both OpenAI-compatible and native modes); operators switch providers in the UI without restarts or code changes. - **Live observability.** Every chat turn, web-search call, and LLM call emits a lineage event that lands in `session_events` and tails in the per-agent **Activity** tab in the admin UI within 5 seconds. - **DB-backed configuration.** The agent SDK fetches its connection bundle from the controller at boot — no platform secrets in the agent's container env. --- ## What's new ### Agent runtime control plane - **`POST /api/spm/agents`** — upload `agent.py` (multipart) with `deploy_after=true`. Validates syntax, top-level `async def main`, and dry-import; mints per-agent `mcp_token` + `llm_api_key`; creates the per-agent Kafka topics; spawns the runtime container; polls for the SDK's `aispm.ready()` handshake. - **`POST /api/spm/agents/{id}/start | /stop`** — idempotent kick; UI surfaces a persistent "working…" spinner until the polled `runtime_state` actually changes. - **`DELETE /api/spm/agents/{id}`** — stops the container, drops the topics, deletes the row. - **`POST /api/spm/agents/{id}/chat`** — full pipeline, SSE response. - **`GET /api/spm/agents/{id}/bootstrap`** — DB-backed SDK boot. The agent's container only needs three env vars (`AGENT_ID`, `MCP_TOKEN`, `CONTROLLER_URL`); everything else is fetched here. - **`GET /api/spm/agents/{id}/policies`** + **`PUT`** — atomic-replace attach/detach. The chat handler reads `linked_policies` per turn and forwards them to OPA so policies can scope evaluation. - **`GET /api/spm/agents/{id}/activity`** — unified timeline (chat turns + `AgentToolCall` + `AgentLLMCall`), newest-first, capped at 200 rows. Polled by the Activity tab. ### Agent-side SDK (`agent_runtime/aispm`) - `aispm.ready()` — lifecycle handshake. - `aispm.chat.subscribe()` / `reply()` — Kafka I/O. Consumer uses `auto_offset_reset="earliest"` so the very first message after deploy is never silently dropped during consumer-group join. - `aispm.chat.history(session_id, limit)` — replay persisted turns; example agents use this for conversation memory across turns. - `aispm.mcp.call("web_fetch", ...)` — JSON-RPC over HTTP to the MCP server; `web_fetch` is Tavily-backed. - `aispm.llm.complete(messages=, model=…)` — OpenAI-compatible call through `spm-llm-proxy`; the SDK no longer pins a default model so the operator's chosen provider model wins. - `aispm.get_secret(name)` — per-agent secret store. - `aispm.log("step", trace=…)` — structured lineage line on stdout. ### Provider dispatch (spm-llm-proxy) | `connector_type` | Endpoint | Auth header | Model source | |------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `anthropic` | `{base_url}/v1/messages` | `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | integration `model` (payload `model` honoured only when it starts with `claude`) | | `ollama` (`/v1`) | `{base_url}/chat/completions` (OpenAI-compatible) | none | payload `model` > integration `model` > `llama3.1:8b` fallback | | `ollama` (other) | `{base_url}/api/chat` (native) | none | payload `model` > integration `model` > `llama3.1:8b` fallback | Switching provider is a UI dropdown change on the **AI-SPM Agent Runtime Control Plane (MCP)** integration row — no restart, no agent re-deploy. ### Observability (`AgentToolCallEvent`, `AgentLLMCallEvent`) - `spm-mcp` emits `AgentToolCallEvent` after every `web_fetch`, capturing tool name, args, ok/error, and `duration_ms`. - `spm-llm-proxy` emits `AgentLLMCallEvent` after every chat-completion call (Anthropic and Ollama paths), capturing model, prompt and completion token counts, and ok/error. - Both events publish to `cpm.global.lineage_events`. The existing `lineage_consumer` persists them into `session_events` automatically. - Best-effort by design: a producer init failure never blocks the serving path. A `lineage_producer.send failed` warning is the only signal when Kafka is unreachable; chat keeps working. ### Admin UI - **Inventory → Agents tab** lists live agents alongside mock rows with a runtime-state pip and risk tint. - **PreviewPanel** (right-side panel on row click) carries the Run/Stop toggle, **Open Chat**, **View Detail**, and **Delete asset** actions. - **AgentChatPanel** (300px inline panel) opens from PreviewPanel's Open Chat. Composer pinned to bottom (`min-h-0` + `max-h(100vh-120px)` so it can never be pushed off-screen by long chat history). - **AgentDetailDrawer** (560px overlay) opens from PreviewPanel's **View Detail** button. Five tabs: Overview, Configure, Activity (live tail, polls every 5s), Sessions, Lineage. - **PolicySelector** lets operators attach/detach policies on a live agent without leaving the panel. - **Add Integration** modal: `enum_integration` fields render as real dropdowns of existing integrations (no more pasting UUIDs). - **Run/Stop button** stays in a "working…" state until the next poll observes the actual runtime-state change. ### Examples A new top-level [`Example agents/`](Example%20agents/) folder ships five ready-to-deploy agents — one per `agent_type` enum value: | File | `agent_type` | Demonstrates | |-------------------------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `custom_agent.py` | `custom` | Bare-SDK happy path with `aispm.chat.history()` conversation memory and a strong web-search prompt. | | `langchain_agent.py` | `langchain` | Off-the-shelf LangChain `AgentExecutor` + `@tool` calling our MCP / LLM proxies. | | `llamaindex_agent.py` | `llamaindex` | LlamaIndex chat-engine routed through `aispm.llm`, with a hand-rolled retrieval fallback. | | `autogpt_agent.py` | `autogpt` | Self-prompting plan → execute → reflect loop, capped at 3 hops. | | `openai_assistant_agent.py` | `openai_assistant` | OpenAI Assistants-style request shape (system + user + tools), no framework. | The runtime image now has `langchain==0.3.*`, `langchain-openai==0.2.*`, `llama-index-core==0.11.*`, and `llama-index-llms-openai-like==0.2.*` baked in, so `langchain_agent.py` and `llamaindex_agent.py` deploy cleanly without bringing your own image. --- ## Bug fixes - **`paused` agent immediately after deploy.** The upload route's `_wait_for_ready` was reading a stale identity-mapped Agent row from its own SQLAlchemy session and timing out, then overwriting the (correctly running) row to `crashed`. Fixed with `db.expire_all()` on every poll iteration. - **First message after deploy silently dropped.** The agent's Kafka consumer joined the group with the default `auto_offset_reset= "latest"`, so any message produced between `aispm.ready()` flipping the row to `running` and the consumer registering with the broker was skipped. Fixed by switching to `earliest`. - **`Prompt blocked by safety guard. (S2)` on the literal word "yes".** Three different code sites (two adapters and one module-level function injected via `guard_fn=`) had the same anti-pattern that forced `verdict=block` whenever any S1–S15 category appeared, even when the guard's own verdict was `allow`. Replaced with a length-based bypass for inputs under `GUARD_MIN_TEXT_LEN=8` chars and a score-threshold (`GUARD_BLOCK_SCORE=0.6`) gate on the category-escalation path. - **502 `Load failed` on chat.** The `agent_chat.py` SSE handler was importing `aiokafka` lazily but the package wasn't in `spm-api`'s requirements. Added the dep. - **500 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'services.spm_api'`** in both `spm-llm-proxy` and `spm-mcp`. Both fell back to a brittle cross-service import. Inlined `_decode_secret` and dropped the cross-service registry lookup so each service is self-contained. - **`POST /v1/chat/completions` returning 500.** The proxy was hardcoded to Ollama's `/api/chat` shape; pointing **Default LLM** at Anthropic produced a 404 from `api.anthropic.com`. Now branches on `connector_type` and translates request + response shape per provider. - **`web_fetch` 404 on `http://spm-mcp:8500/mcp`.** The MCP server registered tools with FastMCP but never mounted FastMCP's HTTP transport. Added an explicit `POST /mcp` JSON-RPC handler. - **`spm-mcp` crashing at startup with `TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class`.** `from __future__ import annotations` in `tools/web_fetch.py` made FastMCP's annotation introspection blow up. Removed. - **`agents.code_blob` self-heal.** Operators who `rm`'d the bind-mount source previously broke the agent permanently. The runtime image now rewrites the file from `agents.code_blob` (DB-stored agent.py source) on every spawn. - **`Integrations` page blank after creating the agent-runtime row.** `OwnerAvatar` crashed with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'split')` when the new row had no owner. Defensive null-name guard. - **`null is not an object (evaluating 'n.id')` UI crash.** The `mergeAgents` / `mergedAllAssets` / `adaptLiveAgent` chain had no null filtering, so a poll race during a failing fetch could leave a null entry in the array.
